**Course source:** Day 1 §5.6. **Running system:** Order, Product, and User services.

## Why one Consul server is insufficient

If the registry is the source of live service endpoints and settings, it needs a failure story. The course distinguishes **server agents** from **client agents** and introduces clustering and the Raft coordination algorithm.

In Consul's server cluster, Raft helps members agree on replicated state, including leadership and committed changes. A majority is generally necessary to commit changes; merely connecting additional client agents does not add voting server quorum.

~~~text
Server A  <--> Server B <--> Server C
                 |
              Client agents
                 |
           Product / Order
~~~

## Understand quorum before scaling

For a three-server voting cluster, a majority of two is needed. If one server fails, the remaining two can normally continue. If a network partition leaves a single server isolated from the other two, it cannot unilaterally commit new cluster state.

This is a coordination-system concept, not a promise that every query fails in every partition; precise read behaviour depends on consistency settings and API semantics.

## Operational tasks

Join members using configured addresses; verify leader election and health; protect gossip and API traffic appropriately; back up state; and monitor leader changes, quorum loss and service checks.

Do not confuse high availability of the registry with high availability of Product. A healthy registry can correctly report that all Product instances are down.

## Design consequence

A microservice architecture needs *both* a control-plane availability strategy (registry, configuration) and a data-plane resilience strategy (timeouts, routing, retries, isolation). The Consul cluster solves only part of the problem.

## Test your reasoning

Name the component that owns this responsibility, explain its behaviour during a failure, and identify one configuration or metric you would verify in production.

## Mathematical Abstraction

Raft-style majority requirements depend on the voting-server count.

$$
q=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor+1
$$

For $n$ voting servers, $q$ is the majority quorum needed for typical committed writes. This does not describe every possible read consistency mode.
